newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber prices steady, poll results awaited.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber prices steady, poll results awaited.

text.p: Thai rubber prices were mostly steady this week, with exporters way of selling pending the results of the general election on November 17, trade sources said on Friday.
Many said local rubber prices could rise if the Democrat Party, whose political stronghold is in the south, wins the election. The south is Thailand's biggest rubber-producing region.
Opinion polls indicated that the Democrats are running a close race with the New Aspiration Party. Traditionally, the party winning most parliamentary seats forms the government.
"Some are reluctant to commit for fears that the local prices might rise," one Bangkok trader said.
"But demand seemed to pick up as buyers sought to cover the demand for the first quarter of 1997," said another trader from Hat Yai.
There have been some buying orders and enquiries from China, Japan and Europe, trade sources said.
Thai benchmark RSS3 for December shipment was quoted around US$1.24-1.26 a kg FOB Bangkok, barely changed from last week.
STR20 for the same shipment was quoted around $1.23-1.24 a kg on Friday from $1.24 last week. Latex edged down slightly to 94 U.S. cents a kg on thin demand.

Political factors aside, traders said they saw export prices moving in their current range until the end of the year as higher demand would be offset by more supply coming to the market after the monsoon season ended.
